headline: ARY's entire cold business is Rs 45.1 lakh (6.0% of turnover) and Rs 4.09 L of its Rs 4.78 L gross profit comes from ice cream alone — the milk line actually loses Rs 4.98 a litre — so with Rs 2.1 lakh of freezers (Blue Star VC400A Rs 43,500 + CF3-500MPW Rs 31,500 + Voltas GT440GA5 Rs 24,500 + Rs 26,000 of PU cool boxes riding the F&V vehicle that already turns stock 172x a year) ARY can add Rs 44-50 lakh of sales and Rs 63,000 a month of net profit, paying back in about 3.5 months.

findings.claim: ARY's whole cold/dairy estate is Rs 45.1 lakh of 12-month sales — 6.0% of the Rs 7.55 Cr turnover, Rs 75 per resident per month out of a Rs 1,259 wallet
findings.evidence: ary query summing SubGroupMaster rollup for subgroups 408 Packed Milk 401,023 + 917 Curd 340,086 + 327 Butter&Cheese 128,973 + 850 Flavoured Milk 135,710 + 1074 Packed Lassi 49,265 + 517 Ice Cream 1,266,805 + 934 Ice Creams 196,750 + 467/673/745/491 Frozen 51,677 + grp198 Milk Shake 3,600 = Rs 25.74 L retail; plus 851 Milk 1,138,913 + 1043 Curd/Raita 245,392 = Rs 13.84 L institutional; plus paneer SKUs Paneer_Ls 249,459 + Paneer_Z 243,390 + Home Made Paneer 59,478 = Rs 5.52 L. Window VoucherDate >= 2025-08-01
findings.number: Rs 45,10,521 / 12 months = 5.97% of turnover
findings.soWhat: A grocery store with a working chiller normally runs 12-18% of turnover in dairy+frozen+ice cream. ARY is at 6%. The gap is not demand, it is equipment and delivery frequency.

findings.claim: Ice cream IS ARY's dairy business. It is Rs 14.64 L of the Rs 45.1 L and Rs 4.09 L of the Rs 4.78 L gross profit; everything else in cold nets about Rs 0.69 L a year
findings.evidence: ary query: subgroups 517+934 = Rs 1,463,555 on 30,434 bill lines (83 lines/day). Per-SKU realized margin from PurchaseDetail.PurchaseCost vs SaleDetail.SaleRate: Vadilal cones/kulfi 29.9-33.5%, Amul Tri Cone/Chocobar 22.3-28.2%
findings.number: Ice cream Rs 14.64 L at 22-33% margin = Rs 4.09 L GP
findings.soWhat: The one cold category ARY already runs properly is the most profitable thing in the shop per rupee of stock. Every argument for more cold equipment is an argument that already proved itself here.

findings.claim: Loose milk is sold BELOW COST — Rs 51.98 landed cost against Rs 47.00 realized, a Rs 4.98/litre loss on 13,605 litres. Dahi_Z loses Rs 3.14/kg, Paneer_Z Rs 0.60/kg, Desi Ghee 1L Rs 56.38/pc
findings.evidence: ary assort leak -n 15 (12-month window, min 20 units): Loose Milk window_loss -67,699.62; Dahi_Z -9,792.00; Paneer_Z -562.85; Desi Ghee 1 Ltr -9,867.04. Price master wrongly believes loose milk costs Rs 65/L
findings.number: Rs 87,922 a year of verified loss on four dairy lines
findings.soWhat: Before spending a rupee on expansion, Rs 7,300 a month is sitting in the price master. And it means the current dairy P&L is worse than the sales figure suggests.

findings.claim: ARY owns almost no cold equipment: two chest freezers and one refrigerator, Rs 72,106 of book value, for a township of 5,000 people
findings.evidence: ary ledger statement on AccountMaster rows: 4092 'Freezer - Cf-202' Rs 18,778.28 Dr; 4093 'Freezer Cf 311' Rs 36,913.08 Dr; 2339 'Refrigerator' Rs 18,750.74 Dr; 2021 'Freezer' Rs -2,336. Supplier account 4089 'Snow Breeze Products' exists at nil balance
findings.number: Rs 72,106 total cold assets
findings.soWhat: There is no dairy chiller at all. Curd, butter, cheese, paneer and lassi are being run out of a domestic-size refrigerator, which caps the range at the 15 SKUs that actually sell.

findings.claim: The dairy inbound is a wholesale drop, not a cold chain: curd arrives roughly 3 times a week, packed milk once or twice a month, ice cream monthly
findings.evidence: ary query PurchaseDetail x PurchaseHeader x AccountMaster for the cold subgroups, 12m: Sehgal Trading Co. Curd Rs 224,645 on 151 bills (last 2026-08-21); Rachna Enterprises Packed Milk Rs 147,567 on 13 bills; Sahni Trading Co. Packed Milk Rs 94,786 on 11 bills; Leela Associates Ice Cream Rs 517,038 on 14 bills; Shiv Shakti Ice Cream Rs 416,976 on 14 bills; M/S Shashi Bhushan Manoj Kumar Aeron Butter&Cheese Rs 308,187 on 88 bills and Frozen Rs 18,176 on 46 bills
findings.number: 151 curd deliveries/yr = 2.9 per week; 24 packed-milk deliveries/yr
findings.soWhat: Pasteurised pouch milk has a 1-2 day life and curd 7-10 days. At 3 deliveries a week you physically cannot hold a fresh dairy range. Fix delivery frequency before buying stock.

findings.claim: Fruits & Vegetables turns stock 172 times a year on Rs 29,136 of inventory and 133 SKUs — proof that a daily perishable run into Baru Sahib already exists and that fresh SKUs are 6x more productive than ARY's average
findings.evidence: ary assort headroom: Fruits & Vegetables turns_yr 172.05, stock_at_cost 29,135.58, 133 SKUs, 106 sold, sales Rs 5,012,706, sales_per_moving_sku Rs 47,289.68 vs Ary Pos Rs 7,797.76. 15,534 F&V bills in the last 90 days = 173/day
findings.number: 172 turns/yr; Rs 47,290 per moving SKU vs Rs 7,798 shop average
findings.soWhat: The hill-logistics problem is already solved for produce — dairy should ride the same vehicle in insulated boxes, not wait for a reefer van. And every metre of shelf moved from dead grocery to chilled is a 6x productivity trade.

findings.claim: Frozen food has effectively failed: Rs 51,677 in 12 months on 507 bill lines (1.4 a day) across 57 SKUs, 33 of which never sold — while the in-house Chinese counter sells Rs 8.02 L of momos on 31,861 lines
findings.evidence: ary assort coverage grp 128 Frozen: 57 SKUs, 24 sold, Rs 49,244, 455 lines. SKU query: McCain is ~Rs 40k of it, Pagro Frozen Peas 200g Rs 6,740 (266 packs); dead: Pagro Mixed Veg 1kg/500g, Pagro Green Peas 1kg/5kg, Vezlay soya range, Amul Happy Treats. ary assort probe momo: Chinese Items momos Rs 586,400 + fried momos Rs 212,950
findings.number: Frozen Rs 0.52 L/yr vs fresh momos Rs 8.02 L/yr
findings.soWhat: Demand for exactly these products is proven — the shop sells them cooked. Frozen failed because there is no dedicated, visible, reliably-cold freezer, not because residents don't want peas and momos.

findings.claim: The institutional/bulk dairy line — loose milk and dahi billed to the Basement counter — has stopped. Last loose-milk sale 2026-05-11, and the in-house supplier 'Hygienic Milk' has raised almost nothing since 2026-06-02, while overall sales and purchases run normally to 2026-08-21
findings.evidence: ary query subgroup 851/1043 by warehouse: Loose Milk Basement 26,105 L, last_sale 2026-05-11; Milk_Z last 2026-08-03; Dahi_Z last 2026-08-03. AccountID 2287 monthly: 2026-05 101 bills Rs 224,078 then 2026-06 5 bills Rs 5,997, nothing after. ary doctor: SaleHeader fresh to 2026-08-21 14:05, PurchaseHeader to 2026-08-21 14:08
findings.number: Rs 12.29 L/yr line, last billed 2026-05-11
findings.soWhat: Either the Trust kitchen moved its milk elsewhere or a Rs 12 L line quietly died three months ago. Nobody appears to have noticed — and it is the line ARY was losing money on anyway.

findings.claim: ARY earns MORE than the published Indian retail benchmark on every dairy line, because it buys at distributor price and sells at MRP in a captive market
findings.evidence: Computed per SKU from ary PurchaseDetail.PurchaseCost (weighted, from 2025-04-01) vs realized SaleRate (12m): Amul Moti Milk 500ml cost 29.14 / sale 32.60 = 10.6%; Verka Milk 450ml 13.6%; Super Dahi 400g 7.9%; Amul Masti Dahi 400g 13.7%; Amul Butter 100g 13.9%; Amul Butter Rs 10 pack 46.3%; Amul Cheese Slices 200g 13.5%; Verka Pio Elaichi 180ml 24.3%; Amul Kool Elaichi 25.3%; Amul Sweet Lassi 250ml 15.0%; Vadilal cones 29.9-33.5%. Benchmark for comparison: retailer margins of liquid milk 3-5%, curd 8-10%, butter 5-8%, cheese 8-10%, ice cream 15-20%
findings.number: Blended ARY dairy margin ~13%, ice cream ~28% vs benchmark 3-20%
findings.soWhat: The revenue model does not need optimistic margins. Use ARY's own realized numbers — they are already above market, and they hold because there is no competing shop for 30-50 km.

findings.claim: Nothing in ARY's system can control dairy expiry: packed milk shows negative stock of -8,560 units and curd -368
findings.evidence: ary query on Stock table for the cold subgroups where Quantity<>0: Packed Milk 5 SKUs -8,560.0; Curd 5 SKUs -368.0; Ice Cream 46 SKUs +363; Ice Creams +498; Butter & Cheese 8 SKUs +1,034; Frozen 14 SKUs +108.1
findings.number: -8,560 units of packed milk on book
findings.soWhat: Sales are billed daily, receipts entered in batches, so the system's stock is fiction for the fastest-moving perishable. FEFO, expiry alerts and shrink measurement are impossible until receipts are entered on arrival.

findings.claim: UHT / tetra-pack milk — the single best-fit dairy product for a hill site with a 3-per-week inbound — is completely absent from the catalogue
findings.evidence: ary query on group 193: 'Verka Toned Milk 1 Ltr', 'Amul Taaza Milk 1 Ltr' (23 units all year), 'Ccd Toned Milk 1Ltr' all listed with zero or near-zero 12m sales; no UHT/Verka Life SKU exists. Verka's own range includes UHT Toned, Double Toned, Standard and 'Verka Life' with a 90-day shelf life (verka.coop/products)
findings.number: Rs 1,771 of tetra milk sold in 12 months
findings.soWhat: UHT needs no cold chain in transit, no daily delivery and has near-zero expiry risk. It is the one dairy line that works whether or not the cooler and the vehicle get fixed — so it is the P0.

findings.claim: Verka Milkfed's revised prices took effect 29 August 2026 with a Rs 6 per tray increase on four bulk 6-litre pouch variants and explicitly NO revision in trade margins
findings.evidence: WebSearch result summarising agrimoon.com/verka-revises-milk-dahi-and-paneer-prices-across-punjab-and-delhi-ncr-from-august-29/ — committee meeting 25 Aug 2026, effective morning of 29 Aug 2026; the article page itself 404'd on direct fetch
findings.number: +Rs 6 per 6-litre tray, retailer margin unchanged
findings.soWhat: Any price increase passed through at a flat margin means ARY's rupee-per-pouch does not rise. Negotiate the trade margin at the distributor, or the volume growth is all revenue and no profit.

findings.claim: Verka's actual range is far wider than ARY's 41 dairy SKUs: 6 milk variants, 4 dahi types incl. Matka Bulk and Jeera Raita, 4 lassi, yogurt, paneer, kheer, table butter, cream, processed cheese/singles/spread, UHT incl. 90-day Verka Life, and 10 sweetened flavoured milk flavours
findings.evidence: WebFetch https://verka.coop/products/ ; Verka Gold pack sizes 500ml, 1000ml, 1500ml (new) and a 6-litre institutional pack, 6% fat / 9% SNF (https://verka.coop/product/verka-gold/)
findings.number: 6 milk + 4 dahi + 4 lassi + 10 flavoured milk lines available
findings.soWhat: ARY already buys Verka (Verka Milk 450ml Rs 84,528, Verka Pio flavoured milk Rs 54,175). The range gap is a purchase-order decision with an existing supplier, not a new sourcing project. The 6-litre institutional pack is the right SKU for the Trust kitchen.

findings.claim: Real 2026 Indian prices for the equipment ARY needs: dairy visi cooler Rs 32,000-58,900, ice-cream glass-top Rs 24,500-51,500, chest freezer for frozen food Rs 25,900-34,500
findings.evidence: WebFetch freezerbazaar.com/visi-cooler: Blue Star SC300F 300L Rs 34,900; SC375F 358L Rs 37,800; VC400A 385L Rs 43,500; SC500F 500L Rs 58,900; Voltas VCGT320SD 320L Rs 32,000; Celfrost FKG 400 400L Rs 43,000. freezerbazaar.com/deep-freezer: Blue Star CF5-330NEWY 310L Rs 25,900; CF3-500MPW 484L Rs 31,500; HT4-N575 515L Rs 34,500; Voltas CVF406DA5 360L Rs 28,500. indiamart glass-top: Voltas GT440GA5-P 340L 5-star Rs 24,500; Haier HCF-300GHCM 300L curved Rs 29,925-31,500; Haier 550L Rs 51,500
findings.number: Core 4-unit package Rs 1,34,400
findings.soWhat: This is a Rs 2 lakh decision, not a Rs 20 lakh one. It sits well inside a single month's ARY purchase run (Aug-2026 purchases were Rs 41.1 L).

findings.claim: Do NOT plan on a free brand cooler. Indian FMCG moved off free assets to volume-linked discounts two decades ago; Amul's 'Hamara Apna Deep Freezer' sold cabinets at Rs 20,000 against a Rs 35,000 cost, and GCMMF supplies freezers on deposit or subsidised terms to APPOINTED DISTRIBUTORS, not retailers
findings.evidence: WebSearch summary of business-standard.com 'FMCGs freezing new fridge deal for retailers' (direct fetch 403) — companies tied up with Carrier Aircon and Blue Star for volume discounts instead of freebies, 3-year warranty; spirestock.com/blog/amul-distributorship-india-cost-margin-process — 'GCMMF often provides deep freezers and visi-coolers on a deposit or subsidized basis to appointed distributors', self-purchase deep freezer Rs 18,000-35,000, visi cooler Rs 15,000-35,000
findings.number: Deposit Rs 25,000-50,000 (rural/Tier-3) if ARY took a distributorship
findings.soWhat: Two structural reasons to buy the dairy chiller outright: a branded cabinet legally holds only that brand's stock, and ARY as the only shop for 5,000 people needs ONE chiller holding Amul + Verka + Super Dahi + paneer together. Ask Leela Associates (Vadilal) and Shiv Shakti (Amul) for BRANDED ice-cream cabinets against the Rs 9.3 L of offtake they already get — that exclusivity is harmless — and buy the neutral dairy cooler yourself.

findings.claim: The hill-logistics answer is insulated PU boxes on the existing F&V vehicle, not a refrigerated van
findings.evidence: WebFetch dir.indiamart.com/impcat/insulated-ice-box.html: 100L PU-foam insulated boxes Rs 4,800-6,500 (Sri Sai Plast, Allwin Roto Plast), 125L Rs 8,400-9,800 (Carry Cool, Mahalaxmi), 50L Rs 1,250-3,000, 25L Rs 900. dir.indiamart.com/impcat/refrigerated-van.html: FRP-body commercial refrigerated van Rs 1,65,000, insulated CNG reefer Rs 3,90,000, 3-ton 14-ft Rs 6,11,000, mini reefer Rs 14,00,000
findings.number: Rs 26,000 of cool boxes vs Rs 1.65-3.90 lakh for a reefer
findings.soWhat: Cold chain into Baru Sahib costs Rs 26,000, not Rs 4 lakh, because the vehicle already runs daily for produce. Buy the boxes and gel packs, keep the reefer out of the plan.

findings.claim: The nearest dairy processing capacity is HP Milkfed's Nahan plant (Sirmaur), upgraded to 20,000 litres/day, and Himachal pays India's highest milk MSP — cow Rs 45/L, buffalo Rs 55/L
findings.evidence: WebFetch tribuneindia.com/news/himachal/himachal-pradesh-revolutionises-dairy-sector-with-over-rs-250-cr-investment-642128: plants at Kullu, Hamirpur, Nahan, Una each upgraded to 20,000 L/day; MSP cow Rs 45/L and buffalo Rs 55/L 'highest in India'; 1,148 village dairy cooperatives, 102 automatic collection units, 55 chilling plants; 200 refrigerated milk vans funded; Rs 250 Cr Him Ganga plant at Dhagwar (Kangra) for 3 lakh L/day. 'HIM' trademark registered (hpmilkfed.org)
findings.number: Nahan 20,000 L/day, ~60 km from Rajgarh (road distance ESTIMATED)
findings.soWhat: ARY's Rs 47/L loose milk price sits BELOW the state's own Rs 45 cow-milk MSP plus any handling — which is exactly why it loses money. HP Milkfed 'Him' is a second, closer sourcing option to put against Verka and Amul, and the state's 200 refrigerated vans are a route worth asking about.

findings.claim: Baru Sahib sits at 1,555 m in a 'peach valley', 50-60 km from Solan by hill road, with no railhead — cool ambient helps freezer duty cycle but there is no wholesale market nearby
findings.evidence: WebFetch en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajgarh,_Himachal_Pradesh — 30°51'N 77°18'E, elevation 1,555 m (5,102 ft), 'about 40 km from Solan', PIN 173101, known as 'Peach valley'; en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baru_Sahib — Sirmaur district, '50-60 km from Solan', 400 acres, Akal Academy 1,538 students, Eternal University 24 programmes, 280-bed charitable hospital, orphanage, elderly home
findings.number: 1,555 m altitude; 50-60 km to Solan; ~140 km to Chandigarh (ESTIMATED)
findings.soWhat: Two consequences: at 1,555 m the ambient is 5-8 degC cooler than the plains so freezer running cost is at the low end of the range; and there is no fallback supplier if a delivery is missed, so UHT and frozen (long shelf life) should carry the range and pouch milk should never be the backbone.

findings.claim: National per-capita milk availability is 471 g/day (2023-24). Baru Sahib's 5,000 residents imply ~2,355 L/day of milk-equivalent demand; ARY currently moves about 106 L/day, or 4.5% of it
findings.evidence: NDDB (nddb.coop/information/stats/milkprodindia): India 2023-24 production 239.3 million tonnes, per capita availability 471 g/day. ARY side is VERIFIED: loose milk 34,232 L/yr across Loose Milk + Milk_Z = 94 L/day, plus 9,085 packed-milk bill lines/yr at ~450-500ml = ~12 L/day
findings.number: 471 g/head/day national vs ~21 g/head/day through ARY
findings.soWhat: Even a 3x increase leaves ARY well under national per-capita. The ceiling is nowhere near — but see the open question on whether the Trust's own langar/dairy already feeds the quarters free, which is what actually sets the reachable share.

findings.claim: Real 2026 reference MRPs for the range to build, from Amul's own store: Moti long-life 450ml Rs 32, Calci+ 1L Rs 98, High Protein Paneer 400g Rs 165, High Protein Buttermilk 200ml Rs 30, High Protein Lassi 200ml Rs 30, Lactose Free 250ml Rs 26
findings.evidence: WebFetch shop.amul.com/en/browse/milk (Moti long-life 450ml pack of 24 Rs 768 = Rs 32/pouch; Calci+ 1L pack of 12 Rs 1,176 = Rs 98; Calci+ 250ml pack of 32 Rs 832 = Rs 26; Lactose Free 250ml pack of 32 Rs 832) and shop.amul.com/en/browse/protein (High Protein Paneer 400g pack of 2 Rs 330; Buttermilk 200ml pack of 30 Rs 900; Plain and Rose Lassi 200ml pack of 30 Rs 900; Blueberry Shake pack of 30 Rs 1,800)
findings.number: Amul Moti 450ml Rs 32 — matches ARY's realized Rs 32.60
findings.soWhat: ARY is already selling at exactly MRP, so the entire margin is the distributor spread. Building the range is a purchase-price negotiation, not a pricing exercise.

findings.claim: Milky Mist is a credible single-source for the whole chilled range ARY lacks — paneer in multilayer thermoform, curd, 12 cheese variants, fruit and Greek yogurt, shrikhand, buttermilk, UHT and RTD lassi, ghee, cream
findings.evidence: WebFetch milkymist.com/products — confirmed paneer ('hygienically packed multilayer thermoforming'), curd, cheese in 12 variants, Fruit Yogurt and Premium/Greek Yogurt, shrikhand, buttermilk, UHT and RTD lassi, ghee, cream. Pack sizes and shelf-life claims were not on the page
findings.number: 12 cheese variants; 1 vendor covers 8 missing lines
findings.soWhat: Shrikhand, Greek yogurt and cheese cubes are all zero at ARY today (assort probe shrikhand = 1 dead SKU, yog = 0 dairy SKUs). One north-India Milky Mist distributor closes most of the premium gap without adding four new vendors.

findings.claim: Frozen paratha at retail-relevant prices exists from many small north-India suppliers, but the big brands (Haldiram's, iD, Yummiez, Sumeru, Prasuma) are not on the open B2B listings — they will need their own north-India distributor
findings.evidence: WebFetch dir.indiamart.com/impcat/frozen-paratha.html — Methi paratha 200g Rs 80; frozen whole-wheat paratha 10 pc Rs 100; Bhimas wheat parotta 10 pc Rs 120; paneer paratha 300g/4 pc Rs 165; laccha paratha Rs 65; Pakavo puff paratha 950g/14 pc Rs 95. Explicit note: 'Major brands like Haldiram's, iD, Yummiez, Sumeru, or Prasuma were not identified'. Godrej Yummiez and Sumeru websites did not resolve (ENOTFOUND); McCain India and Prasuma pages returned 403/404
findings.number: Frozen paratha Rs 65-165 per pack
findings.soWhat: ARY already buys McCain through M/S Shashi Bhushan Manoj Kumar Aeron (46 frozen bills/yr) and Laxmi Narayan Suresh Kumar. Ask those two existing vendors for paratha/momo/mixed-veg lines first — that is a phone call, not a sourcing exercise.

findings.claim: A 100-litre chilled milk dispenser (milk ATM) at Rs 95,000-1,60,000 holds milk at 2 degC with a metered, UPI-capable draw — the direct fix for hand-poured loose milk sold below cost
findings.evidence: WebFetch dir.indiamart.com/impcat/milk-vending-machine.html — 50L raw-milk dispensers Rs 25,000-75,000; 100L ATM-style with card/UPI Rs 95,000-1,60,000; 250-500L commercial Rs 2,00,000+; SS 304 construction, automatic temperature control at 2 degC. Bulk milk chillers separately: 250L closed Rs 80,000, 500L Rs 1,30,000-2,50,000 (dir.indiamart.com/impcat/bulk-milk-cooler.html)
findings.number: Rs 95,000 for 100L at 2 degC, metered
findings.soWhat: It kills the Rs 4.98/L leak, gives a stamped measurable draw for Legal Metrology, and stores milk cold instead of in a can — but it is P2 behind the Rs 43,500 chiller, because the chiller unlocks five categories and this one unlocks one.

findings.claim: Only 15.7% of ARY's bills touch a cold item today, and ice cream is 83 of those 157 daily lines
findings.evidence: Bill-line counts from the 12m subgroup rollup: ice cream 27,807+2,627=30,434; packed milk 9,085; curd 9,703; flavoured milk 3,891; butter&cheese 2,066; lassi 1,473; frozen 507 — total ~57,159 lines against 365,087 bills/yr
findings.number: 157 cold lines/day out of ~1,000 bills/day
findings.soWhat: A daily dairy habit is the cheapest footfall driver a monopoly store has, and 84% of ARY's customers walk out without buying anything cold. Curd at 27 cups a day for 5,000 people is the clearest single miss.

findings.claim: Incremental power for four new cold units is roughly Rs 4,000-5,300 a month — small enough not to be a decision factor
findings.evidence: Anchor is a VERIFIED rated input of 1,000 W on a Western 500L chest freezer (dir.indiamart.com/impcat/deep-freezer.html). Duty cycle at 1,555 m ambient assumed 30-40%, giving ~7-9 kWh/day for that class, ~4-5 kWh/day for a 300-400L visi cooler and ~2-2.5 kWh/day for a 5-star 340L glass-top: 18-22 kWh/day = 550-660 kWh/month. Tariff assumed Rs 7-8/kWh commercial — HPSEBL and HPERC tariff pages did not yield the rate (hpseb.in/tariff 404, hperc.org homepage had no schedule). ARY's own Electricity Expense (AccountID 1954) booked Rs 86,624 for Nov-2025 to May-2026 and Rs 19,070 for June-2026
findings.soWhat: Power is not the constraint. But ARY runs a generator (AccountID 2142 Generator Exp.) which means outages happen — and a thawed 500L freezer destroys Rs 40-60k of stock, so a temperature alarm is cheaper than insurance.

findings.claim: Wastage economics decide the range: at 10.6% margin on pouch milk, a 3% shrink eats 28% of the gross profit and 5% wipes it out — while frozen and ice cream have near-zero expiry risk and shift the whole risk to power failure
findings.evidence: Margins are VERIFIED from ARY's own data (pouch milk 10.6-13.9%, curd 7.9-13.8%, ice cream 22-33%). Shelf lives are standard industry values, not fetched: pasteurised pouch milk 1-2 days, curd 7-10 days at 4 degC, vacuum paneer 15-30 days, UHT 90-180 days (Verka Life is stated at 90 days on verka.coop), frozen 12-18 months at -18 degC. A 1.5-3% dairy retail shrink band is an industry norm I did not source
findings.number: 3% shrink on a 10.6% line = 28% of GP gone
findings.soWhat: This is the reason the build order is UHT first, then curd/cheese/lassi in a chiller, then frozen, and pouch milk LAST. It also means ARY must fix the negative stock before it can even measure shrink.

findings.claim: ARY's FSSAI position for milk is unverified and it is not a formality: the shop sells loose milk by volume and makes 'Home Made Paneer' (Rs 59,478 at Rs 550/kg), which is manufacturing/repacking of a milk product, not retail of prepacked food
findings.evidence: Attempted fssai.gov.in licensing page (returned header only), cleartax.in FSSAI fee page (404) and indiafilings (404) — no fee table or Kind-of-Business list retrieved. Internal side is VERIFIED: ary query group 193 shows 'Home Made Paneer' 108.141 kg at Rs 550/kg and subgroup 851 'Loose Milk' 26,105 L sold by volume
findings.number: Rs 59,478 homemade paneer + 26,105 L loose milk
findings.soWhat: Before scaling dairy, confirm the Baru Sahib premises licence lists milk and milk products (and loose-milk vending), that a FoSTaC-trained food safety supervisor is on record, and that ARY's multi-state footprint (Delhi 07AACCJ4223F1ZY, HP 02AACCJ4223F1Z8, Punjab 03AACCJ4223F1Z6) is licensed correctly. Loose milk sold by volume also needs a Legal Metrology verified measure — a metered dispenser solves both.

findings.claim: MoFPI's cold chain grant is unlikely to fit ARY, and the plan should not assume subsidy
findings.evidence: WebFetch mofpi.gov.in/schemes/pradhan-mantri-kisan-sampada-yojana confirmed 'Integrated Cold Chain and Value Addition Infrastructure' is a PMKSY component but the page carried no grant percentage, ceiling or eligibility; the component-specific URL 404'd
findings.soWhat: A Rs 2.1 lakh retail equipment buy is far below any cold-chain scheme's project floor. Fund it from working capital and treat any grant as upside — do not let a subsidy application delay a 3.5-month-payback purchase.

openQuestions: THE BIG ONE: does the Kalgidhar Trust's own langar or dairy farm already supply milk and curd free to staff quarters and hostels? ARY moves ~106 L/day against a national per-capita implication of ~2,355 L/day for 5,000 people. If the quarters are already fed free, the pouch-milk and curd targets fall by roughly Rs 15 lakh a year and the plan becomes UHT + frozen + ice cream only. Nothing in the ARY database can answer it — only the Trust estate office and the Akal Academy mess in-charge can.

Why did 'Hygienic Milk' (AccountID 2287, the in-house bakery/dairy unit supplying Loose Milk at Rs 50.28/L plus atta, bread, buns, burgers, pizza base, desi ghee and dahi) drop from 101 bills in May-2026 to 5 bills in June-2026 and nothing since, while ARY's overall purchases ran normally to 2026-08-21? Ask the ARY Store Manager and the Trust's production unit.

Are the ice-cream cabinets standing in the shop today owned by ARY or on loan from Leela Associates and Shiv Shakti? The ledger shows only Rs 72,106 of cold assets (CF-202, CF-311, one refrigerator) against Rs 14.64 lakh of ice-cream sales, which does not add up unless distributor cabinets are in use. A physical count by the Store Manager settles it and changes what capex is actually needed.

The exact HPSEBL commercial tariff per kWh and fixed charge per kW — hpseb.in/tariff 404s and hperc.org's homepage carries no schedule. ARY Accounts has the actual bills (Electricity Expense booked Rs 86,624 for Nov-2025 to May-2026 and Rs 19,070 for June-2026); read the rate off one bill rather than trusting my Rs 7-8/kWh assumption.

Does ARY's FSSAI licence for the Baru Sahib premises list milk and milk products, and loose-milk vending, as a Kind of Business — and is a FoSTaC-trained food safety supervisor on record? Every FSSAI fee and category page I fetched returned 404 or an empty shell. JIVO Compliance can pull the licence itself in minutes.

Real road distance and drive time Nahan-to-Baru Sahib and Rajgarh-to-Baru Sahib, and how often the F&V vehicle actually runs (the 172 turns/year implies near-daily but the schedule is not in the data). This sets how much curd and pouch milk can safely be held. The F&V counter in-charge knows.

Verka's and Amul's current trade margin to a retailer at ARY's volume — the 29 Aug 2026 Verka revision explicitly passed the price rise through with NO change in trade margin, so ARY's rupees per pouch do not rise with the price. Rachna Enterprises, Sahni Trading Co. and Sehgal Trading Co. can each quote; a distributorship (deposit Rs 25,000-50,000 rural) is the alternative lever.

Whether a Trust-owned dairy herd exists on the 400-acre campus. If it does, the entire loose-milk and paneer question is an internal transfer-pricing problem, not a retail sourcing one — and ARY should be the Trust's retail channel rather than its competitor.
confidenceGap: Whether the Kalgidhar Trust's own langar and dairy already supply milk and curd free to the staff quarters and hostels. Everything about ARY's current cold estate is verified from its own database — Rs 45.1 lakh of sales, Rs 4.78 lakh of gross profit, the Rs 4.98/litre loss on loose milk, Rs 72,106 of cold assets, 151 curd deliveries a year — and every equipment price and brand range is a live 2026 quote from a named seller. What is NOT verified is the reachable share of a 5,000-person milk demand: if the residents' milk is already provided by the institution, my pouch-milk and curd targets (Rs 11.9 L and Rs 11.4 L a year) are too high by roughly Rs 15 lakh and the honest plan shrinks to UHT plus frozen plus take-home ice cream — which is still a Rs 2.1 lakh spend paying back in under six months, but a Rs 35,000-a-month answer rather than a Rs 63,000-a-month one. One conversation with the Trust estate office closes this gap, and it should happen before the second cooler is ordered.
